name: OpenImageIO
listed_description: Powerful image and texture wrangling library with support for a wide number of common lossy and RAW formats. (awesome-cpp, Image Processing; licence tag Modified BSD)
reason: No numeric comparison against another library. The repo has moved to https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/OpenImageIO (Apache-2.0, 2.4k stars); its README makes no speed claim. CHANGES.md (raw.githubusercontent.com) quantifies speedups only against OIIO's own earlier code: IBA::resample 'speed up 20x or more' (PR 4993, jessey-git table 4096x4096 uint8 PNG 25% resize 282.5 ms main versus 16.9 ms PR, CPU and compiler not stated), resample axis tables 1.9-3.6x (PR 5395, Windows 11, MSVC 14.50, CPU not stated), NEON exp/log 2.5x, maketx --envlatl over 10x. PRs 4993 and 5395 name no OpenCV, ImageMagick or libvips baseline. Two WebSearch queries (oiiotool versus ImageMagick, OIIO versus OpenCV/libvips/OpenEXR) found no head-to-head timing that includes OIIO. Lead: a run of imageinout_test (PR 5037, read/write speed versus tile size) or a libvips vips-bench style harness with OIIO added would give numbers.

name: OpenJPEG
listed_description: An open-source JPEG 2000 codec written in C language. (awesome-cpp, Image Processing; licence tag BSD-2-Clause)
reason: No numeric win over an outside baseline. README says the repository is unmaintained and makes no speed claim; wiki pages Optimization and WhatsNew (opened) have only qualitative notes. Numbers exist only against OpenJPEG's own earlier revisions: PR 786 (multithreaded T1/DWT decode, i5 750, Release, 4 threads: 730 to 359 ms and 3920 to 1310 ms on its test files versus the previous PR 783 revision), PR 945 (T1 flag optimizations, total 23049 to 20172 ms, -12.5%, CPU and flags not stated), PR 1253 (forward DWT, i7-6700HQ, 5-3 vertical pass 7.9 s to 1.7 s). PR 917's Travis log (benchmark script, reference column labelled Kakadu but run.sh sets REF_VERSION=v2.1.2, so the reference may be an older OpenJPEG) shows the then-new build 149.9% slower than the reference, and a CNRS HTJ2K page (merovingio.c2rmf.cnrs.fr, seen only as a WebSearch snippet, not opened) says OpenJPEG is 10x (lossy) to 15x (lossless) slower than Kakadu; a 2007-2010 Second Life mailing-list anecdote (OpenJPEG 0.051 s versus GeoJasPer 0.074 s versus Kakadu 0.025 s) came only from search snippets and list-archives.secondlife.com and ffmpeg.org (2013 libopenjpeg versus FFmpeg native decoder thread) could not be opened (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). Guessed baseline libjpeg is the wrong format. Lead: Second Life 2007 sldev post if the host opens (would be tier C anecdote versus Jasper).

name: OpenSubdiv
listed_description: Pixar's library for evaluating and rendering subdivision surfaces on CPU and GPU (awesome-cpp, Graphics; licence tag Modified Apache2)
reason: No numeric comparison against an outside baseline. README says only 'high performance' with no figures. documentation/release_30.rst (raw.githubusercontent.com) claims 3.0 stencil tables give 'as much as a 4x interpolation speed-up' and initial refinement 'close to an order magnitude' faster, but both are against OpenSubdiv 2.x subdivision tables and Hbr (its own earlier code), with no workload, CPU or GPU named. Other release notes (3.1 to 3.7), far_overview.rst, osd_overview.rst and bfr_overview.rst have no timings. WebSearch snippets only: the AlSub paper (arXiv 1809.06047) benchmarks AlSub against OpenSubdiv with OpenSubdiv as the slower baseline, and Blender bug T73752 reports OpenSubdiv CPU slower in 2.8x than 2.7x; neither page was opened. Category guess color-and-resampling is wrong (subdivision surfaces / geometry). Lead: AlSub paper tables if paper access opens.

name: OpenVDB
listed_description: Library and tools for storing, editing, and rendering volumetric datasets (awesome-cpp, Graphics; licence tag MPL2, now Apache-2.0)
reason: No usable numeric comparison against an outside baseline in reachable sources. README has no speed claim. doc/faq.txt and doc/nanovdb/FAQ.md (raw.githubusercontent.com) say OpenVDB is 'almost always superior' to dense grids 'in our experience' and NanoVDB is 'generally faster' than OpenVDB, with 'only a benchmark comparison can tell you', all without figures. doc/points.txt: 2x to 3x from spatially organised point data versus randomly ordered linear data (internal layout comparison). The root CHANGES file has numbers only against OpenVDB's own earlier code (box filter 10-50x faster, mesh-to-volume 1.5x to 5.5x faster, CRC32 6.5-17x) plus one claim against an outside baseline in release 0.104.0 (February 15 2013): '.vdb files are now saved using a mask-based compression scheme that is an order of magnitude faster than ZLIB and produces comparable file sizes for level set and fog volume grids', with no workload, hardware or method (would be tier C at best, a file-format codec claim, not a data-structure claim). The Museth 2013 ACM TOG paper (research.dreamworks.com), the NanoVDB 2021 talk paper (research.nvidia.com), artifacts.aswf.io, www.openvdb.org and developer.nvidia.com all failed with getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND; arXiv is blocked. Lead: Museth 2013 paper tables versus dense grids and Field3D, and NanoVDB 2021 CPU/GPU timings versus OpenVDB, if those hosts open. Category guess color-and-resampling is wrong (sparse volumetric data structure).

name: Opus
listed_description: A totally open, royalty-free, highly versatile audio codec. (awesome-cpp, Audio; licence tag BSD; listed URL https://opus-codec.org/ not opened)
reason: No numeric speed comparison found. xiph/opus README (raw.githubusercontent.com) and GitHub page have no benchmark data; the only performance text is the -complexity 0..10 setting and a note that fixed-point is slower on platforms with a fast FPU. The NEWS and ChangeLog files at the repo root are empty (0 bytes via raw). Two WebSearch queries (Opus versus libvorbis, FAAC, LAME, fdk-aac encode speed or real-time factor) returned only quality rankings (FFmpeg wiki) and no libopus speed or CPU-complexity numbers. Opus is positioned on quality at low delay and bitrate, not on being faster than other codecs. Lead: the Opus codec papers by its Xiph/IETF authors, not located or reachable here.

name: Panda3D
listed_description: A framework for 3D rendering and game development for Python and C++ (awesome-cpp, Graphics; licence tag BSD; listed URL https://www.panda3d.org/ not opened)
reason: No numeric comparison found. README and repo page (5.2k stars, Modified BSD) have no benchmark; the only performance remark is that building with Eigen may 'improve runtime performance', with no figures. One WebSearch query (Panda3D FPS versus Ogre3D, Irrlicht, Unity, pygame, Godot) found only old forum anecdotes on discourse.panda3d.org and irrlicht.sourceforge.io (for example an ocean demo at about 30-40 fps in Panda3D versus 70-90 fps in Ogre, i.e. Panda3D slower); the pages could not be opened and no engine claims to be faster. Guessed baseline OpenGL or DirectX and category image-codecs are wrong (it is a game engine, not a codec).
